For Appellant : Ms. Amrita Sharma, Advocate.
For Respondent No.4 : Shri Harashmander Rastogi, Advocate appeared on behalf of Shri N.K.Thakur, Advocate.

This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act') has been filed by the Driver and owner of the offending vehicle Truck bearing registration No. CG-04-E-3546 being aggrieved by the award dated 27/03/2019 passed in Claim Case No. 139/2018 by the Ist Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Balodabazaar (C.G.).

entities.text: Ist Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Balodabazaar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Murlidhar vs Chandrakant Mishra on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44854120/
1 Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12876 2.

By the impugned award against a claim of Rs.22,33,000/-, the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.03,76,000/- with 7% interest per annum in favour of the respondents / claimants holding the appellants/driver and owner liable to pay compensation exonerating the Insurance Company on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license.
Challenge in the appeal is on the ground that the driver had valid driving license, photo copy of which is also on record.
However, the same could not be prove by cogent and prudent evidence.
3. Learned Counsel for the appellant submits that initially the license was issued to the driver of the offending vehicle in the year 2007.

The license to drive transport vehicle was issued in the year-2009 and the accident had occurred on 05/09/2011 and the driving license to drive transport vehicle is issued for a period of 03 year in clause (a) of sub-section 2 of section 14 of the MV Act.
Meaning thereby on the date of accident, the driver had valid and effective driving license.
Therefore, the appeal may be allowed and the Insurance Company may be held liable to pay compensation.

4. Learned counsel for respondent No.4 / Insurance Company supports the award and submits that the Tribunal gave a categorically finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license.

Even otherwise, the photo copies had not been verified by the Insurance company which is required to be proved by cogent and prudent evidence which the appellant had failed to prove.
5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and also perused the record with utmost circumspection.
6. The learned Tribunal exhibited the driving license of the appellant/driver as D-1 C.

Prima facie it indicates that the driver had license to drive transport vehicle which was issued from 18/02/2007 and LMV which was issued on 16/07/2007 and motorcycle with gear was issued on 16/07/2007.

The section 14 of the MV Act is here in below:
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12876 14. Currency of licenses to drive motor vehicles-(1) A learner's licence issued under this Act shall, subject to the other provisions of this Act, be effective for a period of six months from the date of issue of the licence.
(2) A driving licence issued or renewed under this Act shall- (a) in the case of a licence to drive a transport vehicle, be effective for a period of three years.
(Provided that in the case of licence to drive a transport vehicle carrying goods of dangerous or hazardous nature be effective for a period of one year and renewal thereof shall be subject to the condition that the driver undergoes one day refrresher course of the prescribed syallabus; and)
Murlidhar vs Chandrakant Mishra on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44854120/
2 (b) in the case of any other licence,-
(i) if the person obtaining the licence, rither originally or on renewal thereof, has not attained the age of (fifty years) on the date of issue or, as the case may be, renewal thereof,-
(A) be effective for a period of twenty years from the date of such issue or renewal;or (B) until the date on which such person attains the age of [fifty years], Whichever is earlier;

(ii) if the person referred to in-sub-clause (I), has attained the age of fifty years on the date of issue or as the case may be, renewal thereof, be effective, on payment of such fee as may be prescribed, for a period of five years from the date of such issue or renewal:] Provided that every driving licence shall, notwithstanding its expiry under this sub-section continue to be effective for a period of thirty days from such expiry.

5. There is a photo copy of the extract of the driving license issued by the DTO, Raigarh which also indicated that the originally license was issued from 16/07/2007 to 15/07/2027 for non-transport vehicle and thereafter a validity for transport vehicle 14/05/2012 to 13/05/2015 it also indicates that the driving license of transport vehicle was subsequently renewed from 14/05/2015 to 13/05/2018.
It indicates that driving license of transport vehicle was not valid from 08/02/2012 to 13/05/2012.

The date of accident is 05/09/2011.
6.

From perusal of the record it appears that the driving license of transport vehicle was initially issued on the year-2009 but evidence in this record whether it was subsequently renewed and was valid on the date of accident is not fairly spelt out.
The driver of the offending vehicle had driving license, the Insurance Company cannot escape his liability.

In order to prove the driving license, this court is of the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12876 the considered opinion that the matter may be remanded back to determined the fact whether the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license on that day or not particularly in view of the photo copies of the license which was filed.

Therefore, the matter is remanded back to learned Tribunal to determined the issue afresh whether the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid and effective driving license on the date of accident i.e. 05/09/2011.

The owner, driver and Insurance Company is at liberty to file documents,
lead evidence and amend pleadings in this regard.
The compensation which has been awarded is not disturbed and Tribunal may also decide the just compensation after noticing to the appellants/claimants.
This court has not express any opinion on with regard to validity of the driving license.
The party shall appear on 03rd May,2024.
The learned Tribunal shall make endevour to conclude the case within a period of six months with cooperation of the parties.
The amount which has been deposited by the appellant in compliance of the Interim Order and as mandatory deposit shall not be recoverable from the claimants.
7. Appeal thus partly allowed.
8. All pending applications are disposed off.
